column3: The Hebrew title is “Of Solomon”; NASB sets “A Psalm of Solomon” in braces before verse 1. Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has futures, “He will judge”; NASB renders them as wishes, “May he judge,” as in much of the psalm.
Close to the Hebrew; “He will judge” is rendered “May he vindicate.”
“They will fear You with the sun” is rendered “Let them fear You while the sun endures.”
Close to the Hebrew; “well-being” is rendered “peace.”
Close to the Hebrew; “may he give to him” is rendered as a passive, “be given to him.”
NASB supplies “the cedars of” before “Lebanon,” and renders “may they blossom from the city” as “may those from the city flourish.”
